conceptZh: 橙是像柳橙一樣明亮的橘黃色
object: a caped action-figure hero with an overlong cape and a capsule that bursts with oranges
morph: a capsule bursts open and juicy oranges roll out and land as the wood radical 木 and the 登 on top of a bowl, forming 橙
creativeAngle: 披風英雄打開扭蛋，一顆顆柳橙噴出來，把他的披風染成橘色；橙子滾落排成「橙」，詞用「柳橙」。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale aqua-white backdrop, locked camera. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 橙, centered in saturated juicy orange strokes about 70 percent of frame height, with the wood radical 木 on the left and the 登 part on the right, with its tent-like top and the 豆 below. Cast: Captain Flop, a chunky caped toy action figure with a bright blue cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head, and a big glossy capsule toy with a twist lid. Moment one, 0 to 1.7s: Captain Flop strikes a heroic pose, steps on his own cape, and spins the big capsule open with both hands. The first 橙 is spoken as the lid pops and a single orange shoots up. Moment two, 1.7 to 3.4s: a stream of round oranges bursts out, bouncing off his helmet and knocking his cape over his face; he does a wide-eyed double-take and catches one in each hand, juggling badly while the rest roll across the floor and line up into the vertical and crossing strokes of 木 on the left. The second 橙 is spoken as the last orange of 木 drops. Moment three, 3.4 to 5.0s: orange peel strips curl into the tent-shaped top of 登, orange slices slide into place as the small steps below it, and a halved orange makes the round bowl-like 豆 at the bottom, each one landing with a juicy bounce while Captain Flop yanks his cape off his face and gapes at the finished character. Moment four, 5.0s onward: he sniffs an orange and sneezes silently. From 5.0 to 8.0s the glyph is perfectly still and uncovered while Captain Flop holds one orange on top of his head like a hat and sways a small happy dance at the bottom of the frame, cape flapping, never touching the strokes. Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「橙、橙、柳橙」, slowly with clear tones as ㄔㄥˊ、ㄔㄥˊ、ㄌㄧㄡˇ ㄔㄥˊ. First 橙 near 0.7s, second near 2.4s, and 柳橙 around 5.3s as he balances the orange on his head. Stop after the word. Only soft pops and bounces, no background music. Soft studio lighting, vivid not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 橙.

conceptZh: 玩具消防車想要高高木箱上的大柳橙，先被亂噴的水管甩飛，再倒退助跑全速撞上木箱「碰」一聲壓扁，震落的木板排成左邊的木、爆開的橙瓣落成右邊的登，最後水管回頭把整台消防車噴成亮橙色。
object: a chunky toy fire engine with a runaway hose, a tall wooden crate, and one giant glossy orange perched on top
morph: the crash shakes the crate apart: its planks drop into the 木 radical on the left, while the giant orange pops up and bursts into peel curls and wedges that fan down into the 登 half on the right
creativeAngle: 上一版是披風英雄開扭蛋，這次改成「衝刺撞擊」的純肢體笑料：消防車先用水管失敗、再倒退助跑撞木箱，字由撞擊震落的木板與爆開的橙瓣直接排成，木旁對應木箱、登對應柳橙，意思與畫面一致；詞選「橙色」，色只有一個讀音最安全，並用水管把紅色消防車噴成橙色，讓聽到的詞在那一秒變成看得到的顏色。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale cream backdrop, locked camera, soft studio lighting. The only text in the whole clip is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 橙, correctly formed with the wood radical 木 on the left and 登 on the right, 登 having its two-flap tent-shaped top and the 豆 shape below. Finished strokes are thick, saturated juicy orange, centered, about 70 percent of frame height, with clear margins.

Cast: Chief Clang, a chunky bright red toy fire engine with big round headlight eyes, a spinning blue roof light and two tiny peg-shaped firefighter figures riding on top. Its hose is a character of its own, wriggling like a mischievous snake. Goal object: a tall wooden crate at the far right with one giant glossy orange perched on top like a trophy.

0 to 1.5s, want it: Chief Clang skids in from the left, headlights go huge, and both crew figures point at the giant orange. The first 橙 is spoken at about 0.7s as the engine leans forward and its roof light spins with excitement.

1.5 to 3.0s, try and miss: one crew figure grabs the hose and aims it at the orange to knock it down. The hose bucks, loops around twice and blasts a jet of water that spins the little figure in a circle and flings him backward onto the ladder, while the orange does not budge. The engine's bumper droops in a frown.

3.0 to 4.4s, the wind-up and charge: the engine backs up to the far left, wheels dig in and spin, the whole body stretches way back like a rubber band, one frozen beat of anticipation, then it rockets right across the frame leaving a dust puff. At 4.3s it slams into the crate with a big squashy BONK, accordion-flat, hubcaps popping off and rolling.

4.3 to 5.2s, the payoff: the crate springs apart and its planks drop one by one into the vertical, crossing and two slanting strokes of 木 on the left. The giant orange pops straight up, bursts open, and its pieces rain down on the right: two curled peel strips land as the tent-shaped top of 登, and fat orange wedges slot into the 豆 shape beneath it, each landing with a juicy bounce. The second 橙 is spoken at about 4.8s as the last wedge clicks in.

5.0 to 8.0s, final hold: the glyph 橙 is complete, perfectly still and uncovered. Down in the bottom left corner Chief Clang wobbles out from under the strokes, flattened and dizzy with a goofy grin and a spiral in each headlight. The hose rears up from the floor, grins, and blasts the red engine with a fountain of bright orange juice so it turns completely orange from bumper to ladder. The word 橙色 is spoken at about 5.8s exactly as the engine changes color. It shakes off droplets, gives a proud blinking-headlight shrug, and the two crew figures high-five on the roof, never touching the glyph.

Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「橙、橙、橙色」, slowly with clear tones, read as ㄔㄥˊ、ㄔㄥˊ、ㄔㄥˊ ㄙㄜˋ. Stop after the word. Only soft cartoon bonks, squeaks and splashes, no music louder than the voice. Vivid but not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no writing other than the single glyph 橙.
